svg.aria-label: How to write ी: one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
svg.title: Writing ी
svg.desc: 3 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ी (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 49 (ी, ii sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 49 of the 91 stored prototypes of the ii sign (54%) draw the arch before the stem, and 44 of those 49 do it in one pen-down run: from the lower tip of the hook, up and over the top, and straight down the stem (43 of the 44 end at its foot). That run is the commonest form, 44 of the 91 (48%); 39 of the 91 (43%) draw the stem first, and 55 of the 91 (60%) draw the whole body without lifting. 29 of the 91 add a short top stroke, after the body in 27: the piece of headline the bundled font prints across the top of the stem (x 0 to 273). The path leaves that piece undrawn, so the strip shows it in grey: in a word it is part of the word's one headline, which native writers draw last, across the whole word (82% of the 2,706 consonant prototypes in the same recognizer). Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant or the headline; the book draws the sign alone and composes no Devanagari word from it. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
